title: Whole-number operations and long division
blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and long-divide whole numbers by hand, write remainders in the form asked, and check every answer.
question: A pharmacy splits 9,270 tablets equally among 45 clinics. How many tablets does each clinic get, and why does the answer need a zero in the middle?

teach.body: Formally, addition and subtraction combine or compare place values (regrouping when a column overflows or runs short), multiplication adds partial products, and long division splits a dividend by a divisor into a quotient and a remainder smaller than the divisor. In plain English: keep every digit in its place column, and check each answer with the opposite operation. On the HESI A2 the wrong options are the answers you get from one dropped digit or one missed borrow.

head: Operation
Key move
Check
teach.caption: The check takes seconds and catches most slips before you pick an option.

items: 4,003 − 1,768: the ones need a borrow, but the tens and hundreds are 0.
Borrow 1 thousand: 4,003 becomes 3 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 13 ones.

teach.caption: Forget the shift and you get 138 + 92 = 230, a classic wrong option.
Repeat until no digits are left. Whatever is left is the remainder, and it must be smaller than the divisor.

items: Divide: 45 goes into 92 two times (90). Write 2 above the 2. Subtract: 92 − 90 = 2.
Bring down 7: 27 is smaller than 45, so 45 goes in 0 times. Write 0 above the 7. This zero holds the tens place.
Bring down 0: 270 ÷ 45 = 6. Write 6. Subtract: 270 − 270 = 0, so there is no remainder.
Answer: 206. Check: 45 × 206 = 9,270. ✓ Without the zero you would write 26, which is 10 times too small.

teach.caption: The stem tells you which form to give. A remainder of 3 is never the decimal .3.

teach.h: Properties that speed up the work
head: Property
Rule
Example
teach.caption: Subtraction and division are not commutative: 12 − 5 ≠ 5 − 12.

teach.text: Four slips the HESI A2 turns into wrong options: dropping the zero in a quotient (9,270 ÷ 45 → 26), turning zeros into 10s without reducing them when borrowing (4,003 − 1,768 → 2,345), not shifting a partial product (46 × 23 → 230), and writing a remainder as decimal digits (14 R 3 → 14.3).

teach.body: Priya Nair, a CNA applying to an LPN program, has 250 gauze pads to pack into kits of 12. Long division: 25 ÷ 12 = 2 R 1; bring down 0: 10 is smaller than 12, so write 0. Quotient 20, remainder 10. She can make 20 full kits with 10 pads left over. Check: 12 × 20 + 10 = 250. ✓ Asked as a mixed number, it would be 20 10/12 = 20 5/6 kits.

items: Line up place values; carry and borrow one column at a time.
Borrowing across zeros: each 0 becomes 9, and only the last place gets 10 more.
Shift each partial product one place left per digit of the multiplier.
Long division: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down; write 0 when a bring-down is too small.
Remainder form follows the stem: R, remainder over divisor, or keep dividing for a decimal.

summary: You can now add, subtract, multiply and long-divide whole numbers by hand, keep zeros in the quotient, and write remainders as R, a fraction or a decimal. You check every answer with the inverse operation, which exposes the dropped-digit options the HESI A2 offers.

A.why: Borrow across the zeros: 5,002 becomes 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 12 ones. 12 − 8 = 4, 9 − 6 = 3, 9 − 7 = 2, 4 − 2 = 2: 2,234. Check: 2,234 + 2,768 = 5,002.

whyNot.0: 2,344 turns each zero into 10 without reducing it to 9 after lending.
whyNot.1: 3,766 takes the smaller digit from the larger in every column instead of borrowing.
whyNot.3: 3,234 forgets that the thousands digit dropped from 5 to 4.

whyNot.1: 406 adds 232 and 174 without shifting the second partial product (it is 58 × 30, not 58 × 3).
whyNot.2: 1,740 is only the 58 × 30 partial product; 58 × 4 = 232 must be added.
whyNot.3: 1,942 drops the carried 3 in 58 × 4 (writes 202 instead of 232).

A.why: 24 ÷ 12 = 2. Bring down 3: 3 is smaller than 12, so write 0. Bring down 6: 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Answer 203. Check: 12 × 203 = 2,436.

whyNot.0: 23 drops the 0 the quotient needs when 3 is too small to divide by 12.
whyNot.1: 230 puts the zero in the ones place; 12 × 230 = 2,760.

B.q: Divide 1,000 by 24. Write the answer as a mixed number in lowest terms.
B.why: 24 × 41 = 984, so 1,000 ÷ 24 = 41 R 16. Remainder over divisor: 16/24 = 2/3. Answer 41 2/3.

whyNot.0: 4 1/6 drops a zero and divides 100 ÷ 24 = 4 R 4.
whyNot.1: 41 3/5 reads the calculator decimal 41.6 as 6 tenths; the remainder is 16 out of 24.
whyNot.3: 42 1/3 rounds the quotient up to 42 and subtracts; 24 × 42 = 1,008 is more than 1,000.

B.q: A clinic bundles 650 patient booklets in packs of 24. How many full packs can be made, and how many booklets are left over?
B.why: 24 × 27 = 648, and 650 − 648 = 2. So 27 full packs with 2 booklets left over.

whyNot.0: A remainder of 26 is larger than 24, so one more full pack can be made.
whyNot.2: 8 left over reads the decimal 27.08 as a remainder of 8; the remainder is 650 − 648 = 2.
whyNot.3: 28 packs would need 28 × 24 = 672 booklets, more than the 650 available.

B.q: Which expression uses the distributive property to find 7 × 48?

whyNot.1: 7 × 40 × 8 multiplies the parts of 48 together instead of adding them (2,240).

C.q: A unit stocks 1,200 alcohol pads and uses 85 pads a day for 12 days. How many pads are left?

whyNot.0: 280 forgets to reduce the hundreds digit after borrowing in 1,200 − 1,020.
whyNot.1: 945 multiplies without shifting the second partial product (170 + 85 = 255), then subtracts.
whyNot.2: 1,020 is the number of pads used, not the number left.

C.q: Divide 9,145 by 45. Write any remainder with R.
C.why: 91 ÷ 45 = 2 R 1. Bring down 4: 14 is smaller than 45, so write 0. Bring down 5: 145 ÷ 45 = 3 R 10. Answer 203 R 10. Check: 45 × 203 + 10 = 9,145.

whyNot.0: 23 R 10 drops the 0 the quotient needs in the tens place.
whyNot.2: 202 R 55 leaves a remainder larger than the divisor 45, so one more 45 fits.
whyNot.3: 230 R 10 puts the zero in the ones place; 45 × 230 is already 10,350.

C.why: 8 × 0 = 0, and 0 ÷ 8 = 0. Zero divided by a nonzero number is 0.

whyNot.0: 0 ÷ 8 = 0; only division BY zero is undefined.
whyNot.2: 8 ÷ 0 is undefined: no number times 0 gives 8.
whyNot.3: 8 ÷ 8 = 1; a nonzero number divided by itself is 1.

reteach.title: Long division is dealing out cash
reteach.question: A bank teller must share $3,672 equally among 12 people using $1,000, $100, $10 and $1 bills. How does dealing out the bills explain every step of long division, including the zero?

blocks.body: There are only 3 thousand-dollar bills, not enough for 12 people, so the teller breaks them into 30 hundreds; with the 6 hundreds that makes 36. Each person gets 3 hundreds. Next come 7 tens: 7 bills cannot go around 12 people, so each person gets 0 tens. That 0 is real: it is the 0 in the answer. The 7 tens become 70 ones, plus 2 ones makes 72, and each person gets 6. Everyone gets $306.

blocks.h: Match each move to long division
items: Breaking bills into smaller ones = bringing down the next digit.
Handing out bills = dividing and multiplying.
Counting what is left in the drawer = subtracting.
Bills that cannot go around = a 0 in the quotient, then break them down and keep going.

blocks.text: Skipping the tens round gives everyone $36, which shares out only $432 of the $3,672. The 0 holds the tens place.

explain.body: When the next place to the left is 0, borrow from the first nonzero digit. Every 0 you pass becomes 9, and only the place that needed the borrow gets 10 more.

whyNot.0: 3,256 turns each zero into 10 without reducing it to 9.
whyNot.2: 4,854 takes the smaller digit from the larger in every column.
whyNot.3: 4,146 forgets that the thousands digit dropped from 6 to 5.

explain.body: Multiply by each digit of the bottom number in turn. The tens digit really means tens, so its partial product shifts one place left (write a 0 first). Then add the partial products.

whyNot.0: 576 adds 448 + 128 without shifting the tens partial product.
whyNot.1: 1,280 is only the tens partial product; 448 must be added.
whyNot.2: 1,708 drops the carried 2 in 64 × 7 (writes 428 instead of 448).

explain.body: After a bring-down, if the number is still smaller than the divisor, the divisor goes in 0 times. Write 0 in the quotient, then bring down the next digit.

test.why: 54 ÷ 18 = 3. Bring down 3: too small, write 0. Bring down 6: 36 ÷ 18 = 2. Answer 302. Check: 18 × 302 = 5,436.

whyNot.1: 32 drops the 0 that holds the tens place.
whyNot.2: 320 puts the zero in the ones place; 18 × 320 = 5,760.

explain.body: To give a decimal, do not stop at the remainder: put a decimal point after the dividend, add zeros and keep dividing. 75 ÷ 4 = 18 R 3, and 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75.

test.q: Divide 75 by 4. Write the answer as a decimal.

whyNot.0: 1.875 places the decimal point one place too far left; 4 × 1.875 = 7.5.
whyNot.1: 18.03 writes the remainder 3 in the hundredths place.
whyNot.3: 18.3 copies the remainder 3 as a decimal digit; 3 left out of 4 is 0.75.
